newsitem.title: UK: Wickes sets premium to rights issue price.
newsitem.headline: Wickes sets premium to rights issue price.

text.p: Shares in do-it-yourself retail group Wickes Plc returned to the market on Monday as a seven-month suspension ended following shareholder approval for a 53 million stg rescue rights issue and capital restructuring.

The stock set an expected premium to the 150p price of the company's rights issue, with the price supported by speculation of a bid from a retailer such as Kingfisher Plc or building materials group such as RMC Plc.
At 0830 GMT, the official start of London trading, the shares were quoted at 200p with volume reaching 44,150 shares.

Wickes shares were suspended at 69p last June after the discovery of accounting irregularities which inflated its profits. Yet after the restructuring, the company's shares are effectively worth a tenth of their former value.
Detailing its restructuring plans last December, Wickes said last December that 150p price of the new shares being issued in its rights issue was equivalent to 15p per existing share.

Last November the company appointed Bill Grimsey as its new chief executive, following the departure of former chairman and chief executive Henry Sweetbaum. Four former senior managers of the company are under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office.
